_description: The Human Tree — multi-axis fractal decomposition of human history. Ring 3: pattern tags as fibers, force decomposition at every level, extensible schema.
_ring_note: Ring 3: Added pattern_tags (cross-cutting fibers with reasons), pattern_tag_vocabulary, force fields on children, event-horizon and leaf types. Same schema at every depth.

sources: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind (Yuval Noah Harari, 2011)
meta.method: Fractal Method — bottom-up decomposition. Multi-axis: structure + time + fiber.
meta.note: Sources array — add new sources as the tree grows beyond any single book.

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: A commonly held belief, origin story, or operating fiction gets overturned
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Barter Economy Myth, Admission of Ignorance, Forager Cultures vs progress narrative

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: One imagined order replaces another through force, persuasion, or obsolescence
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Universal Religions replace polytheism, Nation State replaces Empire

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: An institution, system, or organism fails because it can't scale to its new context
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Agricultural Trap, Empire Trap, Dunbar's Number

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: Destruction, death, or collapse creates the foundation for what comes next
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Failed Empires → infrastructure, Megafauna extinction → ecological niche, Indigenous pruning → ethnobotany

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: A moment after which the previous state cannot be restored
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Cognitive Revolution, Agricultural Revolution, Energy Conversion

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: The tool, system, or practice you adopt ends up capturing you
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Wheat domesticates farmers, Consumerism domesticates desire, Growth Loop

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: The pruned thing is still present — genetically, linguistically, culturally — in the living
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Neanderthal DNA, Dead Languages in living ones, Alchemy in science

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: The simpler version endured longer than the complex one
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Homo Erectus (2M years), Forager Cultures, Fire

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: The actor didn't know — couldn't know — what their action would cause
pattern_tag_vocabulary.examples: Megafauna hunters, Agricultural adopters, Science + Empire symbiosis

pattern_tag_vocabulary.description: The downside IS the mechanism of success. You can't separate them

children.name: The Fiction Engine
children.label: The core mechanism. Sapiens cooperates at scale because it believes in things that don't exist. Every other branch depends on this one.

pattern_tags.reason: Once fictional language emerged, there was no going back to purely biological cooperation. Fiction became the operating system.

children.growth_ring: This is where the fractal begins. Fiction is not a phase — it is the operating system. Money, gods, nations, human rights, corporations: all fiction. All functional.

children.name: Fictional Language
children.label: Not just 'lion at the river' but 'lion is guardian spirit of our tribe.' Fiction enables cooperation beyond Dunbar's number (150).

pattern_tags.reason: The cognitive revolution is the point of no return. Before: biology determines cooperation limits. After: fiction removes the ceiling. Every subsequent revolution depends on this one.
Dunbar's number (150) was the biological limit. Fictional language broke through it — enabling cities, empires, religions. The first scaling break in the tree.

children.growth_ring: The root spark. Before this: biology. After this: culture. The moment gossip became mythology.

children.name: Imagined Orders
children.label: Myths that scale cooperation. First gods, then laws, then constitutions. Each layer builds on the fiction below it.

pattern_tags.reason: Each imagined order replaces the previous one. Polytheism → monotheism → secularism → humanism. The mechanism stays; the content rotates.

children.name: Early Religions
children.label: Animism → polytheism. Gods explain harvest, death, weather. Religion is the first shared operating system.

children.name: Universal Religions
children.label: Buddhism, Christianity, Islam. Local gods replaced by universal orders. One truth for all humanity. Fiction at planetary scale.

pattern_tags.reason: Universal religions didn't just add to local religions — they replaced them. One god killed many gods. The fiction engine consolidates.
Local religions couldn't scale beyond their geography. Universal religions broke through by abstracting god from place.

children.name: The Nation State
children.label: Imagined community at industrial scale. Standardized language, education, military service. The nation replaces the empire as dominant political fiction.

pattern_tags.reason: The nation-state replaced the empire as the dominant political fiction. 'We the people' killed 'divine right of kings.'

children.name: Dead Religions
children.label: Marduk, Zeus, Ra, Odin. Once commanded millions. Now studied as mythology. Pruned, but their DNA is in every living religion.

pattern_tags.reason: Christmas trees are pagan. Sunday is the Sun's day. Wednesday is Woden's day. The dead gods haunt the calendar of the god that killed them.
Universal religions didn't just outcompete polytheism — they actively killed it. Temples demolished, priests executed, festivals rebranded.
Religions that once explained everything became 'mythology' — the word itself is a demotion. Yesterday's truth is today's fairy tale.

children.prune_reason: Replaced by universal religions and secularism
children.soil_contribution: Every living religion carries DNA from its dead predecessors. Christmas trees are pagan. Sunday is the Sun's day.

children.name: Money
children.label: The most universal and efficient fiction ever devised. Shells, silver, gold, paper, digits — the medium changes, the fiction persists. The only story everyone on earth believes simultaneously.

pattern_tags.reason: Once money exists, you can't go back to a moneyless economy. The fiction is too useful. Even communist states kept money.

children.name: Barter Economy Myth
children.label: No evidence barter economies ever existed at scale. A pruned assumption that persists in economics textbooks.

pattern_tags.reason: The barter story is taught as fact in every economics textbook. Anthropological evidence says it never happened. The fiction engine fictions about itself.
Despite being pruned by evidence, the barter myth persists in textbooks. A zombie fiction — dead but still walking.

children.soil_contribution: Reminder that origin stories are often fiction — even in science. The fiction engine fictions about itself.

children.name: Empires
children.label: Akkadian, Persian, Roman, Chinese. Empire is the default political order for most of history. Not an aberration — the norm. Fiction + violence at continental scale.

pattern_tags.reason: Empire's violence and authoritarianism are inseparable from its stability and infrastructure. You can't have Roman roads without Roman legions.

children.name: Failed Empires
children.label: Every empire is eventually pruned. But their infrastructure — roads, languages, laws — becomes soil for the next.

pattern_tags.reason: Roman roads still underlie European highways. Latin still structures law and medicine. The violence is gone but the infrastructure persists.
The British Empire is gone but English is the global lingua franca. The ghost of empire speaks through every international business meeting.

children.soil_contribution: Roman roads still underlie European highways. Latin still structures medical and legal language. Empire decomposes but its infrastructure persists.

children.name: The Pruning Pattern
children.label: Consolidation is the dominant force across all time. Many species → one. Many cultures → fewer. Many languages → fewer. Many religions → fewer. The tree keeps pruning itself.
children.growth_ring: The counter-narrative. History looks like branching. But the deeper pattern is convergence. The tree prunes more than it grows. What it prunes becomes the soil everything else grows from.

children.name: Species Pruning
children.label: At least six human species once coexisted. Now one remains. The first and most complete pruning event.

pattern_tags.reason: Once the other human species were gone, the possibility of a multi-species human world disappeared forever. We can never know what it would have been.

children.name: Neanderthals
children.label: Larger brains, adapted to cold, buried their dead. Not inferior — different. Pruned from main trunk but DNA persists in modern humans.

pattern_tags.reason: 1-4% of non-African human DNA is Neanderthal. The pruned species is literally inside us. We carry our dead cousin's genes.
The myth that Neanderthals were brutish and stupid has been pruned by science. They had art, burial rituals, possibly language. The myth of Sapiens superiority is itself a fiction.

children.prune_reason: Outcompeted or absorbed after Cognitive Revolution
children.soil_contribution: Interbreeding left 1-4% Neanderthal DNA in non-African populations. The tree remembers.

children.name: Homo Erectus
children.label: Most successful human species by duration. Nearly 2 million years. Pruned, but the longevity is in the soil.

pattern_tags.reason: Homo Erectus lasted 2 million years with simple tools and no fiction. Sapiens has been around for 300,000. Complexity is not durability.
Disrupts the myth that evolution trends toward complexity. The simplest human lasted longest.

children.soil_contribution: Proof that success is not about complexity. Simplicity endured longer than anything Sapiens has built.

children.name: Denisovans
children.label: Known from a single finger bone and DNA. Ghost branch — barely visible but genetically confirmed.

pattern_tags.reason: Tibetan altitude adaptation gene (EPAS1) came from Denisovan interbreeding. A species known from one bone still gives gifts to living humans.

children.soil_contribution: Tibetan altitude adaptation gene (EPAS1) came from Denisovan interbreeding. The ghost still gives gifts.

children.name: Homo Floresiensis (Hobbits)
children.label: Tiny humans on Flores island. Island dwarfism. Survived until after the Agricultural Revolution elsewhere.

pattern_tags.reason: Smaller bodies, smaller brains, survived 88,000 years on a single island. Adaptation to constraint, not growth, was their survival strategy.
Disrupts the myth that bigger = better in evolution. Island dwarfism is adaptation, not degeneration.

children.soil_contribution: Evolution is not a ladder. Smaller can be adaptive. The tree branches in every direction, not just up.

children.name: Ecological Pruning
children.label: Sapiens prunes everything it touches. Megafauna, forests, ecosystems. The most efficient pruner the biosphere has ever produced.

pattern_tags.reason: Early Sapiens had no concept of extinction. They hunted what was there. The ecological devastation was entirely unintentional — and entirely predictable in hindsight.

children.name: Megafauna Extinction
children.label: Giant sloths, mammoths, diprotodons. Pruned within centuries of Sapiens arrival on each continent.

pattern_tags.reason: The extinction of megafauna opened ecological niches that Sapiens filled with domesticated animals. The mammoth's death made room for the cow.
No hunter planned the extinction. Each kill was rational. The cumulative effect was invisible until it was irreversible.

children.prune_reason: Hunted to extinction by newly arrived Sapiens
children.soil_contribution: First evidence that Sapiens is an ecological force, not just another species. The pattern starts here.

children.name: Cultural Pruning
children.label: Agriculture, empire, and globalization compress thousands of cultures into fewer, larger ones. The human story looks like diversification but the deep pattern is consolidation.

children.name: Forager Cultures
children.label: Diverse, adapted, often healthier than farmers. The original affluent society. Pruned by agriculture, wisdom in soil.

pattern_tags.reason: Disrupts the myth of linear progress. Foragers worked fewer hours, had better nutrition, more varied skills. By many metrics, agriculture was a step backward.
Forager lifestyles lasted 58,000 years (cognitive revolution to agriculture). Agriculture has lasted 12,000. The simpler model has the longer track record.

children.prune_reason: Agriculture outcompeted by volume, not quality
children.soil_contribution: Evidence that 'progress' is not linear improvement. Foragers worked fewer hours, had better nutrition, more varied skills.

children.name: Nomadic Pastoralists
children.label: Alternative to farming: follow the herds. Viable for millennia, gradually squeezed by expanding farms.

pattern_tags.reason: Disrupts the myth that agriculture was the only option. Pastoralism was a viable, parallel path that scaled differently.

children.soil_contribution: Proof that agriculture wasn't the only viable path. The tree had more than one option — it chose the one that scaled.

children.name: Indigenous Cultures
children.label: Thousands of cultures, languages, knowledge systems pruned by colonial expansion. The largest pruning event since the species pruning.

pattern_tags.reason: Colonial genocide and forced assimilation destroyed thousands of cultures. The soil — ethnobotany, land management, oral traditions — is immeasurably rich and mostly unexamined.
Colonizers didn't understand what they were destroying. Indigenous knowledge systems — pharmacology, ecology, agriculture — are only now being recognized as sophisticated.

children.soil_contribution: Ethnobotany, indigenous land management, oral history traditions. The soil is immeasurably rich. Most of it is still unexamined.

children.name: Dead Languages
children.label: Sumerian, Latin, Sanskrit, Aramaic. Thousands of languages pruned. Patterns persist in descendants and loanwords.

pattern_tags.reason: English is Latin + Germanic + French + Norse. Every living language is a graveyard of dead ones. The ghosts speak through us every day.

children.prune_reason: Imperial and cultural dominance by successor languages
children.soil_contribution: Every living language is soil from dead ones. English is Latin + Germanic + French + Norse. The tree remembers every pruned tongue.

children.name: Scaling Traps
children.label: Every mechanism Sapiens adopts to grow ends up growing Sapiens. The trap is the feature. Wheat domesticated humans. Consumerism domesticated desire. The tool always captures the user.

pattern_tags.reason: The trunk-level insight: scaling traps are not bugs. They ARE the mechanism of growth. You can't have agriculture's food surplus without agriculture's drudgery. Inseparable.

children.growth_ring: The deepest structural pattern: the Agricultural Revolution was history's biggest fraud. Not because agriculture is bad — but because the thing you adopt to scale always scales you. The pattern repeats with every revolution.

children.name: The Agricultural Trap
children.label: History's biggest fraud. More food per acre, worse life per person. Population explodes, individual quality of life declines. The trap is irreversible — you can't go back once you've grown.

pattern_tags.reason: Once population grows to depend on agriculture, you can't revert to foraging. The trap closes behind you.
More food = more people = more food needed = more work. The surplus creates the dependency. The benefit IS the trap.
Wheat captured humans. Farmers serve wheat's reproductive interests — planting, watering, weeding, protecting. Wheat's DNA spread worldwide by enslaving its cultivators.

children.name: Domestication (Both Directions)
children.label: Wheat, rice, maize, sheep, goats, cattle. But who domesticated whom? Wheat spread its DNA worldwide by enslaving farmers to its schedule.

pattern_tags.reason: The foundational example. Humans thought they domesticated wheat. Wheat's genome spread to every continent. By the metric of reproductive success, wheat domesticated us.

children.name: Permanent Settlements
children.label: Villages, granaries, property. The concept of 'mine' is born. Social hierarchy follows storage. You can't own things if you can't stay put.

pattern_tags.reason: Once you build granaries, you need guards. Once you have guards, you have hierarchy. Once you have hierarchy, you can't go back. Each step locks in the next.

children.name: The Empire Trap
children.label: Empire is the default political order — not the exception. Once you build one, you can't unbuild it without building another. The pattern of capture at civilizational scale.

pattern_tags.reason: Empire's authoritarianism is inseparable from its stability. You can't have Pax Romana without Caesar. The peace requires the emperor.
Every empire reaches a size where its governance model breaks. The Roman Republic couldn't govern a continent. The British Empire couldn't hold after two world wars.

children.name: The Consumerism Trap
children.label: The ethical revolution nobody noticed. Medieval: luxury is sin. Modern: spending is duty. The economy needs you to want. Desire becomes obligation.

pattern_tags.reason: Consumerism captured desire itself. Wanting is no longer a feeling — it's an economic function. The system needs you to want, so it manufactures wanting.
Economic growth requires consumption. Consumption requires desire. The trap (manufactured wanting) IS the engine of growth.

children.name: The Growth Loop
children.label: Credit bets on the future. Science promises the future will be better. Together they create a loop that must keep growing. The trap: you can never stop.

pattern_tags.reason: Credit (the tool) requires growth (the outcome). Once you fund science with credit, you need science to produce growth to repay the credit. The loop captures both.
The growth loop has produced unprecedented material wealth. It has also made perpetual growth obligatory. You can't step off a treadmill while it's running.

children.name: The Ignorance Revolution
children.label: The moment the tree discovered it could observe itself. Pre-science: holy books have all answers. Science: we don't know — let's find out. 'I don't know' becomes the most powerful sentence in history.

pattern_tags.reason: Once you admit you don't know, you can't go back to pretending you do. Science is irreversible — not because knowledge can't be lost, but because the METHOD of doubting can't be unlearned.
Science disrupted the oldest myth of all: that the answers are already known. Every holy book, every tradition, every elder's wisdom — all provisional once 'I don't know' becomes respectable.

children.growth_ring: The tree grows eyes. Science is not a body of knowledge — it is the admission that knowledge is incomplete. The only revolution that starts with surrender.

children.name: The Admission of Ignorance
children.label: Pre-science: holy books have all answers. Science: we don't know, let's find out. The most revolutionary idea in human history is 'I might be wrong.'

pattern_tags.reason: The admission of ignorance disrupted every existing knowledge system simultaneously. If 'we don't know' is valid, then 'we already know' is suspect.
Once the method of systematic doubt exists, every claim must defend itself against it. The pivot from 'received truth' to 'tested truth' cannot be undone.

children.name: Science + Empire Symbiosis
children.label: Science needed funding (empire). Empire needed technology (science). Cook's voyage carries astronomers and botanists alongside marines. Knowledge and power travel together.

pattern_tags.reason: Scientists on colonial voyages didn't intend to enable genocide. But the knowledge they gathered — maps, resources, weaknesses — was weaponized by the empires that funded them.
Science's power comes from its alliance with power. The funding that enables discovery also directs it. You can't separate the knowledge from the patron.

children.name: Writing & Numbers
children.label: Sumer invents writing for accounting, not poetry. The first data structure. Memory escapes the brain. The prerequisite for science — you can't accumulate knowledge you can't record.

pattern_tags.reason: Writing was invented to track debts and grain. It captured human memory — once you can write, you must write. Records become obligations. The tool creates the bureaucracy.

children.name: Alchemy & Astrology
children.label: Precursors to chemistry and astronomy. Pruned as pseudoscience, but their methods — observation, experimentation, record-keeping — are the soil of modern science.

pattern_tags.reason: Newton was an alchemist. Kepler was an astrologer. The scientific method grew from alchemical practice. The tree's eyes evolved from blind groping.
Alchemy was 'disrupted' by chemistry. But the disruption was partial — the methods survived, only the conclusions were pruned.

children.soil_contribution: Newton was an alchemist. The scientific method grew from alchemical practice. The tree's eyes evolved from blind groping.

children.name: Energy Regimes
children.label: Fire → agriculture → animal power → fossil fuels → nuclear. Each energy transition transforms everything above it. The tree runs on decomposed ancient trees. The literal botanical metaphor.
children.growth_ring: Fossil fuels are infrastructure earth from 300 million years ago. Ancient forests, decomposed, compressed, burned to power new growth. Energy IS the metaphor made real.

children.name: Fire
children.label: The first energy regime. Cooking shrinks guts, grows brains. Fire clears land, scares predators, becomes the first tool that transforms the environment, not just the user.

pattern_tags.reason: Fire has been continuously used for 800,000 years. No other technology comes close. The simplest energy regime is the most durable.
Cooking shrank human guts and grew human brains. The biological change was irreversible — modern humans literally cannot survive on a raw diet.

children.name: Agricultural Energy
children.label: Sunlight → plants → calories → labor. The energy regime that feeds billions but traps its operators. More energy per acre, more work per person.

pattern_tags.reason: Agricultural energy captured human labor. Farming requires more work per calorie than foraging. The energy source demands more from its operators than the previous one.

children.name: Energy Conversion
children.label: Heat → movement → electricity. The single most important technical discovery. Not new energy sources — new conversion. The ability to transform one form of energy into another changes everything.

pattern_tags.reason: Once you can convert energy forms, every previous energy regime is unlocked. Heat becomes motion becomes electricity. The pivot that enabled everything after 1800.

children.name: Fossil Fuels
children.label: Coal, oil, gas. Decomposed ancient forests, compressed over 300 million years. The tree literally burns ancient trees to grow faster. Infrastructure earth as fuel.

pattern_tags.reason: Fossil fuels ARE ancient infrastructure earth. Forests that died 300 million years ago, compressed into fuel. The tree burns its ancestors to grow.

children.name: The Happiness Paradox
children.label: The persistent challenge: does any of this make anyone happier? More power, more capability, same suffering. The tree grows but doesn't know if growth is good.

pattern_tags.reason: The happiness paradox disrupts the foundational myth of modernity: that progress = improvement. If agriculture, industry, and information haven't made us happier, what was it all for?

children.growth_ring: The tree questioning its own growth. This branch has no resolution — it's the open question at the canopy edge. If the tree could feel, would it choose to have grown?

children.name: The Forager Baseline
children.label: Fewer hours worked, better nutrition, more varied skills, richer social life. The baseline against which all 'progress' must be measured. By many metrics, it's been downhill since.

pattern_tags.reason: The forager lifestyle lasted 58,000 years. Agriculture has lasted 12,000. By duration alone, the simpler model is winning.
The 'nasty, brutish, and short' myth of pre-agricultural life has been disrupted by anthropological evidence. Foragers were healthier, worked less, and had richer social lives.

children.name: The Progress Illusion
children.label: Each revolution promises improvement. Agriculture: more food (but worse health). Industry: more goods (but worse air). Information: more connection (but worse attention). The promise always partially lies.

pattern_tags.reason: The progress illusion disrupts itself with each revolution. More food didn't mean better food. More connection didn't mean deeper connection. The pattern repeats.
Each revolution's benefit comes packaged with its cost. You can't have industrial abundance without industrial pollution. The progress and the price are the same thing.

children.name: Self-Designed Evolution
children.label: Sapiens begins to design its own evolution. Gene editing, AI, brain-computer interfaces. The next branch hasn't grown yet. We're standing at the tip.

pattern_tags.reason: If Sapiens modifies its own genome or merges with AI, the resulting species is no longer Sapiens. The pivot point is approaching — and it cannot be undone.

children.name: The Information Age
children.label: Current growth edge. Data, networks, AI. The tree begins to model itself. Every prior force — fiction, pruning, scaling, ignorance, energy — converges here. We are here.
children.growth_ring: The growth edge. All six forces visible simultaneously. Fiction runs on servers. Pruning is algorithmic. Scaling traps are platform-shaped. The tree can see its own rings.

children.name: Computers & Networks
children.label: Turing machines, ARPANET, the internet. Information moves at light speed. Geography becomes optional. The fiction engine gets fiber-optic veins.

pattern_tags.reason: The internet broke the scaling limit of information distribution. Before: knowledge travels at the speed of ships. After: at the speed of light. Every prior institution was designed for slow information.

children.name: Globalization
children.label: One economy, one culture? Or one trunk with a thousand branches? The tension between unification and diversity — the pruning pattern at planetary scale.

pattern_tags.reason: Globalization's connectivity is inseparable from its homogenization. You can't have a global market without eroding local economies. The connection IS the compression.

children.name: Biotechnology & AI
children.label: Sapiens begins to design its own evolution. Gene editing, AI, brain-computer interfaces. The tree reaches for its own roots. The ignorance revolution turns inward.

pattern_tags.reason: AI is the latest tool that may capture its user. We built it to serve us. The question is whether it will domesticate us the way wheat domesticated farmers.

infrastructure_earth.description: Pruned branches whose soil feeds current growth. Nothing is lost — only composted. Organized by pruning pattern, not by era.
infrastructure_earth.tagline: The tree remembers what linear history forgot.

existing.test_question: Does compression show in the Sapiens trunk? Can you see cognitive revolution at center, information age at bark?
Where are events densest? Scientific revolution onward should be visibly compressed in time.
Can Sapiens be navigated as nested fractal space? Fiction Engine inside Root?
Do terms align across civilizations? Money, god, law — same function, different names.
Does the compression/expansion cycle map to empire rise/fall?
Can causal loops show how science funds empire funds science?
Can trade routes and idea transmission be built as mesh?
Can full NDD be applied to Sapiens as narrative-driven decomposition?
